relevance_reason: Case report of a child with PEPD and an SCN9A mutation inherited from her father, with phenotypic variability and treatment response.

findings.statement: Meglič et al. (2014) described a 3-year-old girl with an unusual presentation of PEPD: extremely painful voiding (micturition) that had been present since birth. Her father had occasionally had some pain in his jaw while yawning since childhood.
quotes: Here we describe a 3-year-old child with a rare clinical picture of PEPD. Extremely painful voiding had been present since the child's birth.
The same mutation was also found in the girl's father, who has occasionally had some pain in his jaw while yawning since childhood.

findings.statement: In a 3-year-old girl with PEPD presenting with painful micturition, Meglič et al. (2014) identified a heterozygous c.554G>A (p.Arg185His) mutation in the SCN9A gene, inherited from her mildly affected father, who also carried the mutation. The authors noted that the same mutation had been found in patients with small fiber sensory neuropathy, and suggested that intra- and interfamilial phenotypic diversity associated with gain-of-function Nav1.7 variants may explain their case.
quotes: The diagnosis was confirmed by the detection of a heterozygous pathogenic mutation in the SCN9A gene, c.554G>A (p.Arg185His) inherited paternally.
The case is interesting because the same mutation as that found in the girl and her father has been found in patients with small fiber sensory neuropathy.
intra- and interfamily phenotypic diversity in symptoms associated with a gain-of-function variant of Na(V)1.7 are also described and may explain our case

findings.statement: Meglič et al. (2014) reported that carbamazepine significantly reduced pain in a 3-year-old girl with PEPD and painful voiding.
quotes: Significant reduction of the pain was achieved with carbamazepine.

relevance_reason: An international case series that describes the clinical phenotype of paroxysmal extreme pain disorder in 77 people from 15 families.

findings.statement: Fertleman et al. (2007) described the clinical phenotype of 77 individuals from 15 families with paroxysmal extreme pain disorder. Clinical details were collected through an international consortium, and 14 affected individuals completed a validated pain questionnaire. Onset was in the neonatal period or infancy, and the disorder persisted throughout life. Early on, autonomic features predominated: all patients had skin flushing, and most had harlequin color change and tonic attacks. Dramatic syncopes with bradycardia, sometimes with asystole, were common.
quotes: Seventy-seven individuals from 15 families were identified. The onset of the disorder is in the neonatal period or infancy and persists throughout life.
Autonomic manifestations predominate initially, with skin flushing in all and harlequin color change and tonic attacks in most. Dramatic syncopes with bradycardia and sometimes asystole are common.

findings.statement: Fertleman et al. (2007) reported that, later in life, the disorder was marked by attacks of excruciating deep burning pain. The pain was often in the rectal, ocular, or jaw areas but could also be diffuse. Attacks were triggered by defecation, cold wind, eating, and emotion.
quotes: Later, the disorder is characterized by attacks of excruciating deep burning pain often in the rectal, ocular, or jaw areas, but also diffuse.
Attacks are triggered by factors such as defecation, cold wind, eating, and emotion.

findings.statement: Fertleman et al. (2007) found that carbamazepine was effective in almost all patients who tried it, but the response was often incomplete.
quotes: Carbamazepine is effective in almost all who try it, but the response is often incomplete.

findings.statement: Fertleman et al. (2007) noted that paroxysmal extreme pain disorder is most likely to be misdiagnosed as epilepsy. In infancy in particular, it may be misdiagnosed as hyperekplexia or as reflex anoxic seizures.
quotes: It is most likely to be misdiagnosed as epilepsy and, particularly in infancy, as hyperekplexia and reflex anoxic seizures.

findings.statement: Fertleman et al. (2007) used the name paroxysmal extreme pain disorder for the condition previously called familial rectal pain syndrome. They described it as an autosomal dominant sodium channelopathy involving SCN9A.
quotes: paroxysmal extreme pain disorder (previously called familial rectal pain syndrome), an autosomal dominant condition recently shown to be a sodium channelopathy involving SCN9A.

relevance_reason: This paper identified SCN9A mutations as the cause of PEPD and characterized the channel defects they produce.

findings.statement: Fertleman et al. (2006) described paroxysmal extreme pain disorder (PEPD), formerly called familial rectal pain, as an inherited condition characterized by paroxysms of rectal, ocular, or submandibular pain with flushing.
quotes: Paroxysmal extreme pain disorder (PEPD), previously known as familial rectal pain (FRP, or OMIM 167400), is an inherited condition characterized by paroxysms of rectal, ocular, or submandibular pain with flushing.

findings.statement: Fertleman et al. (2006) proposed the name paroxysmal extreme pain disorder (PEPD) for the condition previously known as familial rectal pain (FRP).
quotes: Paroxysmal extreme pain disorder (PEPD), previously known as familial rectal pain (FRP, or OMIM 167400)

findings.statement: Fertleman et al. (2006) carried out a genome-wide linkage search followed by mutation analysis of the candidate gene SCN9A, which encodes the sodium channel Nav1.7. They identified 8 missense mutations in 11 families with PEPD and in 2 sporadic cases.
quotes: A genome-wide linkage search followed by mutational analysis of the candidate gene SCN9A, which encodes hNa(v)1.7, identified eight missense mutations in 11 families and 2 sporadic cases.

findings.statement: Fertleman et al. (2006) tested 3 of the mutant Nav1.7 channels in vitro and found reduced fast inactivation, which led to a persistent sodium current. By contrast, SCN9A mutations that cause primary erythermalgia are associated with more negative activation thresholds. The authors concluded that PEPD and primary erythermalgia are allelic disorders with distinct biophysical mechanisms and represent a separate class of peripheral neuronal sodium channelopathy.
quotes: Functional analysis in vitro of three of these mutant Na(v)1.7 channels revealed a reduction in fast inactivation, leading to persistent sodium current.
Other mutations in SCN9A associated with more negative activation thresholds are known to cause primary erythermalgia (PE).
PEPD and PE are allelic variants with distinct underlying biophysical mechanisms and represent a separate class of peripheral neuronal sodium channelopathy.

findings.statement: Fertleman et al. (2006) noted that carbamazepine is effective in PEPD but not in primary erythermalgia. In vitro, carbamazepine selectively blocked the persistent current of the PEPD mutant channels but did not affect the negative activation threshold of a primary erythermalgia mutant.
quotes: Carbamazepine, a drug that is effective in PEPD, but not PE, showed selective block of persistent current associated with PEPD mutants, but did not affect the negative activation threshold of a PE mutant.
